page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 32.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier across most standard compute and memory tests. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a stress-ng single-core score of 1435.0 and a multi-core score of 15316.01. Memory bandwidth tests show 853.47 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 87.94 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 37.05 GB/sec for large-block writes. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 12.43 GB/sec and handles 15.25 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

For specialized tasks, the CPU supports AVX, AVX512F, and AVX512_VNNI instruction sets, which assist in vector calculations and cryptographic operations. The instance demonstrates moderate capability in software compilation with a Geekbench Clang score of 13543.0, and handles small-scale language model inference, processing 935.61 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model. However, performance drops significantly on larger models, with a weak prompt processing speed of 23.1 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.hfc6.4xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile for CPU-bound workloads. It is well-suited for web serving, database operations, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a cost-effective choice for workloads that do not require high-speed local disk I/O or hardware acceleration.
